claims.text: The current FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size distribution of 15–45 μm.
The current deposition process produces a bond coat thinner than required.
The baseline bond-coat thickness is 15–45 μm.
The baseline coating has a lamellar microstructure influenced by different particle melt states.
The proposed intervention is to replace the 15–45 μm feedstock with a 45–75 μm feedstock.
Feedstock preheating or increased spray energy will ensure that the coarser particles melt completely.
Fully molten particles with sufficient velocity form well-flattened and bonded splats.
Larger fully molten droplets form thicker individual splats and therefore increase coating buildup per pass.
The greater mass and momentum of larger particles improve droplet–substrate impact and splat formation.
Larger particles have a shorter in-flight time, which reduces oxidation.
Preheating or spray-energy optimization promotes complete melting and proper intersplat bonding.
Using the adjusted 45–75 μm feedstock will increase total coating thickness relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The modified process will produce uniform, well-bonded splats with minimal as-sprayed oxidation and preserved microstructural integrity.
The increased thickness will meet the requirements for effective bond-coat performance in a thermal-barrier system.
The intervention should remain effective under standard spray parameters, an inert argon atmosphere, and a room-temperature substrate.
Changes in spray energy, stand-off distance, substrate conditions, or oxygen exposure may require process re-optimization.

contradictions.description: The conditions and experimental design say that spray parameters are otherwise identical, while the intervention permits optimizing spray energy. If spray energy is changed rather than only feedstock preheating, the processes are not otherwise identical and particle size is not isolated as the controlled variable.
